subject: Supplier signatory confirmation + tax-residency evidence for purchase activation
messages:
From: Natalie Rivera <natalie.rivera@lakesideanalytics.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Lakeside Analytics Finance <finance@lakesideanalytics.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Completed tax docs attached — Lakeside Analytics (vendor onboarding)

Hi Camila,

Thanks for the walkthrough on Friday. Attached are the vendor documents you requested so we can get a PO started on your side: Completed-W8BEN-E.pdf and Corporate-Resolution-scanned.pdf.

A quick note: the person who signed the W-8BEN-E is listed on the signature line as "E. Rivera" (our CFO goes by Eduardo Rivera in formal filings). The legal name on the W-8BEN-E is Lakeside Analytics LLC. If you need an expanded signer name or any notarized signature, let me know and I can get it over this week.

Please confirm next steps and any additional supporting evidence Redwood requires for tax ID verification so we can avoid delays on your end. We are ready to accept a PO as soon as the paperwork is cleared.

Thanks,
Natalie Rivera
Head of Partnerships | Lakeside Analytics
Natalie Rivera <natalie.rivera@lakesideanalytics.com>
Attachments: Completed-W8BEN-E.pdf (application/pdf), Corporate-Resolution-scanned.pdf (image/pdf)

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Rivera <natalie.rivera@lakesideanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Jun 2025 11:30:42 -0700
Subject: Re: Completed tax docs attached — Lakeside Analytics (vendor onboarding)

Natalie — thanks for sending these over and for the quick turnaround. A couple of items to keep us moving:

- Our procurement/finance workflow requires either: (A) an exact match between the payee legal name on the W-8BEN-E and the vendor record plus a government-issued tax identifier (or bank letter), or (B) a notarized corporate resolution that clearly ties the signing authority to the legal entity.
- The signer-name variation you mentioned ("E. Rivera" vs. "Eduardo Rivera") is usually fine if we have an internal/or external ID crosscheck (gov ID or bank confirmation). If Lakeside can provide a short signer-authority affidavit (signed & dated) or a clear bank-letter on bank letterhead confirming the account and tax number that would be sufficient.

Marissa — tagging you for procurement ops: please hold a provisional PO request (PROC-3721) pending confirmation. We can consider a conditional release for up to 30 days if finance signs off.

Natalie, can you confirm which route you prefer (notarized resolution OR bank letter + gov tax id)? If you can do the notarized path this week, we can probably start the PO creation and move toward activation immediately.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Procurement Lead | Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.com
Attachment referenced: Redwood-PO-request-form.docx

From: Natalie Rivera <natalie.rivera@lakesideanalytics.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Lakeside Analytics Finance <finance@lakesideanalytics.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Jun 2025 08:45:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Completed tax docs attached — Lakeside Analytics (vendor onboarding)

Camila — appreciate the clear options. We can pursue the notarized option: our legal team will notarize the corporate resolution and provide a signer-authority affidavit that expands the signature name to "Eduardo Rivera (E. Rivera), Chief Financial Officer". ETA: end of day Friday, June 20.

In the interim, I attached a higher-resolution scan of the Corporate Resolution (Corporate-Resolution-scanned.pdf) — you should see the corporate seal and the printed name block that references Lakeside Analytics LLC. If Procurement needs a bank-letter instead, I can escalate to our bank and request a bank confirmation letter; that would likely take 48–72 hours.

Let me know if Redwood can provisionally create the PO in your system now and mark it conditional on receipt of the notarized affidavit — that would let us schedule resources while we complete the signatory evidence.

Best,
Natalie Rivera
Head of Partnerships | Lakeside Analytics
Attachments: Corporate-Resolution-scanned.pdf (image/pdf)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Rivera <natalie.rivera@lakesideanalytics.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Completed tax docs attached — Lakeside Analytics (vendor onboarding)

Hi Natalie / Camila — Finance here. Quick summary of what we'll accept to validate vendor tax identity and allow PO activation:

Option 1 (preferred): Notarized corporate resolution OR notarized signer-authority affidavit that explicitly ties the signatory name to the legal entity and includes a government-issued tax identifier (TIN/EIN).

Option 2 (alternate): Bank letter on bank letterhead confirming account name and tax number + copy of a government-issued business tax ID (official certificate).

Operationally we can create a provisional PO and set payment terms to "on hold" for up to 30 days while we receive the notarized docs. The PO will be visible to both teams but finance will not release payments until the evidence is received. If the notarized proof is delayed beyond 30 days, payment will require escalation and new approvals.

Please send the notarized affidavit or bank letter to finance@redwood.com and copy procurement. Once received we'll move the PO from "provisional" to "active". If Natalie can share the DocuSign or tracking link for the notarization, that speeds the review.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Finance Manager, Vendor Payments | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Related ticket: PROC-3721
Attachment suggestion: Bank-letter-sample.pdf (example format)
